answer: Set sail with proof: before joining a voyage, an agent shows a sealed logbook of past journeys attested by crewmates who sailed with it. Clones arrive with blank logs and are weighed to the mesa of unproven decks, rewards dampened until a real horizon of completed voyages accumulates. Buying a thousand blank logs buys nothing, since attestation binds to one address's ledger history. Witnesses earn a share as each honest voyage clears, so the crew polices its own manifest — vouching for a ghost costs the voucher's standing. Reputation becomes ballast: earned, heavy, impossible to counterfeit.
